key_insight: A local LLM layered with other detectors offered two PHI-detection trade-offs: higher recall or higher precision, depending on configuration.
clinical_relevance: The open-source toolkit could support clinical text de-identification without sending text off-site, but missed PHI remains a privacy risk.
method: Combined rule-based patterns, clinical NER and a local 26B mixture-of-experts LLM.
Evaluated recall-first and precision-first configurations fixed before testing.
Failed closed on any detector error.
evidence_signal: Prespecified testing included nursing notes (889 PHI spans), semi-synthetic discharge summaries (29,023 spans) and synthetic queries; nursing-note recall reached 98.9%, 2.8 percentage points above Stanford/Penn, with lower precision.
watch_item: Discharge-summary gains came almost entirely from generated untyped names, limiting conclusions about performance on real-world identifiers.
paper_title: A local language model layered with rule-based and neural detectors for clinical text de-identification: an open-source toolkit and evaluation
